summary: Ugyen Pelgen is a scholar in Tibetology and history/archaeology. He earned his Master's degree from Aligarh Muslim University and served as a lecturer of History at Sherubtse College.

Ulrich Pagel is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied under Tadeusz Skorupski, Philip T. Denwood, and Renate Söhnen-Thieme, and held a post at SOAS University of London (attested 2013–2020).

Ulrich Timme Kragh works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He studied at Karmapa International Buddhist Institute and the University of Copenhagen, later serving as professor at Geumgang University (2008–2010) and associate professor at Copenhagen (~2014).

Ulrich von Wilamowitz-Moellendorff was a linguistics and history/archaeology scholar. He studied at Schulpforta, Bonn, and Berlin under Otto Jahn, Johannes Schmidt, and Moriz Haupt. He held professorships at Greifswald (1876–1883), Göttingen (1883–1897), and Berlin (1897–1921).

Ulrike Roesler is a scholar of Tibetology, Indology, and Buddhist studies. After earning her PhD at the University of Münster and teaching at Marburg and Freiburg, she became Professor of Tibetan and Himalayan Studies at Oxford (attested 2019).

Uma Chakravarti is a historian and Indologist who studied at Banaras Hindu University and the University of Delhi under D. Devahuti. She served as an educator at Miranda House, University of Delhi, from 1966 to 1998.
Umakant Premanand Shah was a scholar in Indology and history/archaeology. He served at the Oriental Institute, Vadodara, as deputy director in 1954 and head of the Ramayana Project in 1965.

Unnikrishnan Payyappallimana is a scholar of Indology who studied at Bharathiar University and the University of Amsterdam. His career includes posts at FRLHT (1995), Amala Institute, and the University of Toyama as visiting associate professor (2003–2004).

Unrai Wogihara was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He studied under Junjirō Takakusu and Ernst Leumann, obtaining a degree from Strasbourg in 1908. He served as professor at Shukyo University (~1908–1926) and Taisho University (~1926–1937).
Unshō Shaku was a Buddhist studies and religious studies scholar who studied at Mount Koya in 1844. He later founded Kairitsu Gakkō and established Juzen-kai in 1884.

Uranchimeg B. Ujeed is a scholar of Buddhist and Iranian/Central Asian studies. She completed her Ph.D. at SOAS University of London and worked as a Research Associate in the Mongolia and Inner Asia Unit at Cambridge.

Uranchimeg Tsultem is an art historian of Buddhism and Tibetology who earned her Ph.D. at UC Berkeley (~2003–2009). She taught at the National University of Mongolia and was named Fehnel Chair at Indiana University Indianapolis in 2019.

Urs App is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology. He earned his Ph.D. from Temple University under Yoshitaka Iriya and Seizan Yanagida, later serving as Associate Director at Hanazono University's IRIZ from 1989 to 1999.

Ute Hüsken specializes in Indology and religious studies. She earned her doctorate at Göttingen under Heinz Bechert and completed her habilitation at Heidelberg. She was a professor at Oslo (2007–2017) before joining Heidelberg University as professor in 2017.

Utz Podzeit was an Indologist who earned his Dr. phil. from the University of Vienna (1965–1972). He served as Universitätsdozent at Vienna starting in 1969 and undertook a research stay at the University of Madras (1972–1974).

V. Raghavan was an Indologist who earned his Ph.D. at the University of Madras under S. Kuppuswami Sastri. He spent his career at Madras (1934–1968; professor from ~1951) and founded the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute.

V. Venkatachalam was an Indologist who studied at Madras and Nagpur universities. He directed the Scindia Oriental Research Institute (~1972–1985), headed Sanskrit at Vikram University (1974–1985), and served as vice-chancellor at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University and Kameshwar Singh Darbhanga Sanskrit University.
V. Venkayya was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar who studied at Madras Christian College and the University of Madras from ~1880 to 1885, later succeeding Eugen Hultzsch.
Vaibhav Singh is an Indology scholar who earned his PhD from the University of Reading by 2017 and held a post at the same institution, attested in 2018.

Valdo H. Viglielmo was a scholar of Japanology and philosophy who studied at Harvard (A.B. 1946, M.A. 1951–1956). He taught at Harvard, Princeton, and several Japanese universities before serving as Professor at the University of Hawaiʻi (1965–2002).
